meta.owner-order: worktrees and feature branches with the whole process DAG when getting work so it follows a deterministic path with clear checklist runbooks playbooks documents everything that node needs is there and graceful recovery, always, doc design first with those mermaid and build to spec and keep the idea of terraform in mind, the state file is the source of truth, so should the DAG doc design architecture
meta.tool-choice: jq state file under a mkdir lock; Terraform not used because no provider exists for tickets, leases or seats and the graph is under 15 nodes

rule.name: state-is-truth
rule.text: The run state file is the source of truth. Scripts read it before acting and write it after, through dag-lib.sh only.
rule.good: A resumed seat reads state.json and continues on the node recorded there.
rule.never: A script that decides where the run is from a seat's memory or a chat message.

rule.name: atomic-write
rule.text: Write a temp file in the same directory, validate it against the schema, rename it over the old file, all under the run lock.
rule.good: A crash mid-write leaves the old valid file.
rule.never: An in-place edit that can leave half a file.

rule.name: serial
rule.text: Every write increments serial; a writer whose serial is behind aborts with DG-STATE-STALE and re-reads.
rule.good: Two siblings finish together; both proofs land after a re-read.
rule.never: A last-writer-wins overwrite that drops a proof.

rule.name: retry-bound
rule.text: A node retries at most 3 times with its declared waits, then DG-FAILED and DG-HANDOFF. A non-idempotent node never retries blindly.
rule.good: A flaky CI job passes on attempt 3 and the ledger shows the two failures.
rule.never: An unbounded loop, or a silent failure that leaves the run looking healthy.

rule.name: inputs-by-config
rule.text: Every script takes inputs from dag.json and arguments; every Make target passes VAR=value.
rule.never: A path or run id typed into a script body.

rule.name: drift-reports-values
rule.text: Drift prints each mismatch with the state value and the world value, and never repairs.
rule.never: A drift line with no values.

rule.name: merge-never-park
rule.text: N9 merges as soon as N8 is green and the design approval is on record. Build tickets are cut so no ticket waits on an unmerged one more than one deep.
rule.good: CI turns green and dag-merge.sh merges within one poll.
rule.never: A green PR left open to batch with the next one.

rule.name: handoff-with-evidence
rule.text: When a node is DG-FAILED, apply files a fix ticket carrying the reproduction command and its output, then the seat steps aside. A bug without a reproduction is not reported.
rule.good: Ticket body holds the failing command, its exit code and last 40 log lines.
rule.never: A ticket that says "N5 is flaky" with nothing attached.

rule.name: worktree-per-run
rule.text: Every run owns one worktree and one feature branch, opened in N2 and removed in N10. Nothing commits to the base branch.
rule.good: Two runs on two tickets work at once in two worktrees.

state.field: fixed at init, detects a copied state file
per node: status, version, attempts, input, input_sha256, output, output_sha256, error_code, started_at, ended_at, proofs

verb.name: plan
verb.output: plan on stdout: node, class, what it will run

verb.name: apply
verb.output: state updated; one ledger row per node run

steps.step: set up to JOBS ready nodes DG-RUNNING
run each node script; on success write output, hashes, proofs, DG-DONE
on failure retry per the node, then DG-FAILED and DG-HANDOFF

verb.name: drift
verb.output: one DR line per mismatch with state and world values
verb.checks: design worktree lease ticket pr ci output

steps.step: check the lock; a stale lock whose holder is gone is cleared with an unlock ledger row
a node left DG-RUNNING with no live seat becomes DG-READY if idempotent, else DG-BLOCKED with a drift report
for a dead build seat: seat-watch resume or hot swap; new seat gets the node bundle and the last checkpoint
